programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: Mistakes Can Happen At Any Time On Site
programme.desc: This video documents my first-ever cabinet installation for a paying client — from cutting melamine sheets in the workshop to scribing fillers on site and figuring things out the hard way. I walk through the entire cabinetry process: breaking down materials, sizing parts, installing drawer hardware, fixing mistakes, and dealing with walls that are nowhere near plumb. If you’re interested in cabinet making, furniture building, or starting a small woodworking business, this project shows what the job actually looks like — not just the clean highlight reel. This was the last project of 2025 for me, and a big learning curve — especially around quoting install time, managing client expectations, and understanding where profit actually comes from in cabinetry work. If you’re growing a trade business, thinking about taking on installs, or just curious how cabinet makers price jobs, this one’s for you.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: The Most Expensive Plywood I've Ever Worked With
programme.desc: I’m building a custom L-shaped shoe rack using premium Tasmanian Oak veneered plywood with a solid Victorian Ash seat. This project was a great client commission and a fun build, but with timber prices skyrocketing—and Victorian Ash becoming harder to source after the 2023 logging ban—it definitely pushed the limits of my margins. If you’re interested in furniture making, woodworking commissions, or want to see what it’s like working with high-end Tasmanian Oak plywood, this video walks through the full process: design, cutting, joinery, assembly, and installing the solid timber seat. I also talk about pricing custom furniture and how difficult Victorian Ash is becoming to find now that legislation has restricted harvesting.

programme.title: Robin Lewis Makes
programme.sub-title: The Most Beautiful Desk I've Ever Built
programme.desc: Ever thought about making a desk out of end grain? In this video, I take the idea of end grain parquet flooring and flip it on its head — turning it into a custom end grain desk build made entirely from timber offcuts. I walk through the full process of milling, gluing, pattern design, and flattening — essentially creating an end grain board on a massive scale. Along the way, I dive into the big question every woodworker faces: can you glue wood that moves to something that doesn’t? From concerns about wood movement, moisture, and cracking, to experimenting with epoxy and creative inlay work, this project became a long-term experiment in how far you can push the rules of woodworking. Watch the full video to see how I turned a pile of offcuts into a functional, geometric end grain desk — and find out if it actually survived.

programme.desc: Step into greatness as Andrew Nicholson talks about being selected by the Orlando Magic as 19th overall pick in the 2012 NBA draft. He is one of Canada’s most inspiring basketball exports and he sits down for an exclusive interview with True Tv Plus at the world’s only NBA Courtside Restaurant. From his early days with the Orlando Magic, to suiting up for the Washington Wizards and Brooklyn Nets, and now dominating the global stage in KBA, Nicholson opens up like never before. In this rare, intimate conversation, he shares the highs, the heartbreaks,how to eat like a pro, and the mindset that’s fueled his evolution on and off the court. Set against the backdrop of an immersive NBA experience, this is more than an interview; it's a front-row pass into the mind of a man who never stopped believing. Whether you're a die-hard basketball fan or simply love a story of resilience and reinvention, you don’t want to miss this.

programme.title: The Herbert Macaulay Affair
programme.desc: The Herbert Macaulay Affair is a story that follows Young Herbert who returns from England and begins the opposition to the colonial government In 1898, Herbert is done with his scholarship training and becomes the first Engineer and Surveyor in the colony. Upon his return he is employed by the Colonial Government in Lagos He faces a lot of discrimination and watches it being done to fellow Lagosians. Annoyed by the constant marginalization, Herbert quits his job with the colonial government and starts a long opposition to them. He meets a beautiful woman Caroline Pratt who he falls madly in love with and unfortunately loses her to death during childbirth. Herbert is devastated and when he emerges from that darkness he delves more into fighting for independence. Our film catalogues a series of historical events which ends with him going to England to represent the Oba at the Privy council despite the colonial government doing everything to stop him. Car chases, Intrigues, schemes, nationalism and family are all part of this intense 90 minutes movie William Benson plays the Title character Herbert Macaulay. A veteran actor of many theatrical performances. He is well-beloved by a lot of Nigerians mostly because of his role as General Ape in the critically-acclaimed primetime drama Ajoche. He has garnered a cult following and delivers an Oscar-worthy performance in our film The Herbert Macaulay Affair

programme.title: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins Bitcoin 2026 Fireside Chat
programme.desc: For the first time in history, a sitting SEC Chairman took the stage at the Bitcoin Conference. Paul Atkins joins Perianne Boring of The Digital Chamber on the Nakamoto stage in Las Vegas to detail a complete 180 in how the agency views digital assets. He breaks down the new joint token taxonomy with the CFTC, the SEC's reinterpretation of the Howey Test, and the upcoming innovation exemption that will let firms experiment with on-chain securities and token fundraising in the United States. If you want to understand where U.S. digital asset regulation is actually heading, this is the conversation.

programme.title: Fireside: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For more than a decade, Bitcoiners and developers have lived under regulatory uncertainty and sometimes outright hostility from Washington. In this fireside conversation, CFTC Chairman Mike Selig joins Gregory Xethalis to explain how the agency has used its first 100+ days to end regulation by enforcement, launch Project Crypto with the SEC, and protect software developers building on Bitcoin. Selig breaks down the new joint taxonomy guidance, the no-action letter for self-custodial wallets, and why pending market structure legislation is essential to future-proof the asset class.

programme.title: Code is Free Speech: Ending the War on Bitcoin | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For years, Bitcoin developers wrote code with one eye over their shoulder. That era is officially over. At Bitcoin 2026, Coinbase Chief Legal Officer Paul Grewal sits down with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel to break down the April 7, 2025 DOJ memo that ended regulation by prosecution and what it means for builders, platforms, and the future of digital asset policy in the United States. They get into Tornado Cash, Samourai Wallet, the FBI's offshore scam compound takedowns, and why both DOJ leaders are personally Bitcoin holders.

programme.title: Arthur Hayes Bitcoin 2026 Keynote: 21 Weeks Later
programme.desc: The Iran war, AI replacing knowledge workers, and a new Fed Chair pick have markets confused. Arthur Hayes thinks most macro analysts are reading the tea leaves wrong. In this presentation, the BitMEX co-founder walks through why he's turned bullish on Bitcoin, why Kevin Warsh isn't the hawk people fear, and how a quiet April 1st banking regulation could unleash trillions in fresh credit. Hayes lays out a year-end Bitcoin target of $125,000 and explains the wartime money-printing thesis driving him there

programme.title: From American Hashrate to Wall Street: How Bitcoin Benefits The U.S. | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: Bitcoin just crossed the bridge into Wall Street and the boomer money is finally moving. In this Bitcoin Conference panel, Bloomberg's Eric Balchunas sits down with Eric Trump of American Bitcoin and John Koudounis of Calamos Investments to unpack the $60B Bitcoin ETF wave, the $146 trillion in advised assets still sidelined, and the $124 trillion generational wealth transfer about to reshape every portfolio. Eric Trump tells his debanking story and explains why the Trump Organization went all-in on Bitcoin. John Koudounis breaks down Calamos' 100%, 90%, and 80% protected Bitcoin ETFs.

programme.title: Mark Moss: Building a Personal Treasury with a Perpetual Bitcoin Machine | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: You bought the right asset, but are you playing the wrong game? At Bitcoin Vegas 2026, Mark Moss of Market Disruptors argues that most Bitcoiners are still operating with a fiat mindset and will quietly lose the wealth game even with Bitcoin in cold storage. He unpacks the Cantillon effect, the macro debt loop, and a five-step "Perpetual Bitcoin Machine" designed to build a personal treasury that compounds for generations. If you've ever wondered how much Bitcoin you need to retire, this talk reframes the entire question.

programme.title: Merging Traditional Finance with Blockchain Innovation | Alok Sinha from Pazalabs
programme.desc: Join us for an insightful sponsored episode of The Edge of Show as we welcome Alok Sinha, Founder and Chief Ecosystem Officer at Pazalabs. In this episode, we dive deep into the world of real-world assets (RWAs) and how blockchain technology is revolutionizing capital markets. Discover how they are addressing inefficiencies in loan origination, securitization, and liquidity through innovative solutions like AI automation and compliant fractionalization. We explore the complexities of creating a full lifecycle asset commerce ecosystem, the importance of risk and compliance, and how Pazalabs is bridging the gap between traditional finance (CeFi) and decentralized finance (DeFi).

programme.title: AI Produced Bad Crypto!
programme.desc: We asked AI to be the show producer this week by picking the top 10 stories in crypto — and to our surprise, it actually did a pretty great job. Joel and Travis react to a packed lineup of stories including Kraken securing a Fed master account, Nasdaq and Kraken teaming up on tokenized stocks, the ongoing disappointment around the U.S. Bitcoin reserve, the Trump meme coin circus getting another pump, stablecoins quietly taking over the rails of global finance, and Bitcoin outperforming gold during an actual war. Along the way, they talk about why stablecoins may be one of the biggest long-term crypto stories, how banks are fighting to slow down change, why tokenized assets keep getting closer to the mainstream, and whether AI might actually be better than humans at pulling together a useful crypto news rundown. It’s fast, topical, opinionated, and loaded with the usual Bad Crypto mix of market takes, jokes, sidebars, and chaos.

Joel and Travis react to a packed lineup of stories including Kraken securing a Fed master account, Nasdaq and Kraken teaming up on tokenized stocks, the ongoing disappointment around the U.S. Bitcoin reserve, the Trump meme coin circus getting another pump, stablecoins quietly taking over the rails of global finance, and Bitcoin outperforming gold during an actual war. Along the way, they talk about why stablecoins may be one of the biggest long-term crypto stories, how banks are fighting to slow down change, why tokenized assets keep getting closer to the mainstream, and whether AI might actually be better than humans at pulling together a useful crypto news rundown. It’s fast, topical, opinionated, and loaded with the usual Bad Crypto mix of market takes, jokes, sidebars, and chaos.

programme.title: Flying Over Iceland II
programme.desc: Experience the wonders of summertime in Iceland from an elevated perspective with "Flying Over Iceland II: Summer in the Golden Circle". Filmed during quarantine in September of 2020, ambient film features an immersive slow-moving aerial perspective of some of Islandia's most iconic and famous south coast loop locations - all in glorious sunlight. Beginning at the stunning 200 foot high Skogafoss waterfall, viewers next are gently flown to the charming coastal city of Vik, which overlooks the famous Vikurfjara Black Sand Beach. Here ancient lava flows have sculpted some impressive coastal outcroppings which viewers will witness from a bird's eye view, before soaring to great heights in order to witness the distant glaciers and unique geography of South Iceland as never seen before. From the black sand beach we then soar west to the charming Dyrholaey Lighthouse, which also sits atop some absolutely stunning coastal rock formations including a giant arch at sea level. After returning to Vik the film next progresses to the glacier Vatnajökull, offering majestic views of Iceland's largest glacier. From soaring above the misty clouds to dipping down into the ice formations, the film ends with multiple unique perspectives of the glacial area including young pine forests, a visit from some local sheep, and a journey above and below the clouds for one final refreshing cap to the 1 hour film.

programme.title: Rainbow Reef Relaxation 2
programme.desc: Sit back, relax and enjoy the dazzling world of coral reefs in 4K you embark on a journey through some of the most vibrant underwater reefs on our blue planet - including many scenes which no longer look like this due to coral bleaching. From the cinematographer: "The footage for this film was shot over a period of some years in French Polynesia, Micronesia, Indonesia and East Timor. Unfortunately there are not that vibrant anymore today. Coral reefs have suffered from the rise of water temperature, rise in acidity, destructive fishing methods and severe storms caused by climate change." - Peter Schneider. "Rainbow Reef Relaxation" is a 3-hour long, sweeping yet majestic & vibrant underwater journey to the world's most beautiful lagoons, as captured by Nature Relaxation collaborator Peter Schneider (Underwatercam) paired with ambient underwater sounds and brand new ambient music by the Cynic Project. Filmed in High Definition several years ago, thanks to its age this film offers magical glimpses of an underwater world that is bursting with life, color, and beauty.

programme.title: Dive Site Batu Bolong South, Komodo National Park, Indonesia Trailer
programme.desc: Embark on an amazing journey to explore the wonders of Batu Bolong south, a remote and enchanting diving location in Komodo National Park. Dive into crystal-clear waters with excellent visibility to encounter a vibrant array of marine life and stunning underwater landscapes. However, navigating the challenges of strong currents and varying depths requires careful preparation and diving experience. From the captivating giant trevally to the intricate social structures of anthias, you'll observe fascinating behaviors and adaptations of the underwater world's inhabitants. The documentary also sheds light on the unique coral reefs, their crucial symbiotic relationships, and the serious threats they face. This highlights the urgent need for conservation efforts to protect these vital underwater ecosystems often referred to as the "rainforests of the sea." Ultimately, this episode provides a captivating and educational glimpse into the incredible marine life and underscores the importance of preserving these precious underwater environments.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Dos Ojos, Tulum, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Dos Ojos is located 15 kilometers north of Tulum. Dos Ojos (Two Eyes) refers to two neighboring cenotes that are connected by a large cavern that also connects to a subterranean river. The original explorations of this water system, one of the largest in the world, started in the Dos Ojos cenotes. The total length of the combined system was measured at 310.95 kilometers (193.22 mi). This cenote dive site consists of two independent circuits: The first dive starts at the Barbie Line, a 415 meters line with wide spaces and large light galleries. The second dive circuit is called the Bat Cave, a very different experience. The Bat Cave is an adjacent cenote, next to Dos Ojos, and represents a much more preserved environment, mainly due the fact that the roof of the cenote hasn’t collapsed yet and all of the formations around it are in very good shape.

programme.title: Dive Site Siaba Besar, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Siaba Besar dive site is located in the Central part of the Komodo National Park. Siaba Besar dive site is a sheltered bay with coral seamounts and amazing coral reefs, located in the North-West side of the island. The reef is 4-6 meters deep with healthy corals and sand patches around. It has a massive coral garden and lacks strong currents, but it does not mean it lacks cool sights and marine life, just the opposite! This feature makes Siaba Besar a suitable dive site for any kind of level, being the best place for those who have never dived and want to try this amazing experience in Komodo National Park. Siaba Besar is heaven for snorkelers, given its easy conditions with shallow coral reefs, very little current and abundant marine life. A superlative snorkeling among sea turtles it is guaranteed, which gives the nickname to this site: Turtle City

programme.title: Dive Site Tatawa Kecil, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Tatawa Kecil is located in the north-east part of Komodo Island. Tatawa Kecil is known for having strong current, as it is in the middle of the Linta strait, the strait between Komodo Island and Rinca Island. Tatawa Kecil is offering intriguing rock formations, caves, swim throughs, boulders, drop offs, and a massive field with huge and vibrant coral gardens. The topography of the site differs greatly from other ones, it is one of the most fascinating and unique in the park. It has almost anything a diver can hope to see, both big and small, an enjoyable dive is guaranteed.

programme.title: Dive Site Manta Point, Nusa Penida, Indonesia
programme.desc: In this episode, you will explore Manta Point, located in Nusa Penida, Bali, Indonesia, and learn about its remarkable marine inhabitants. Manta Point, situated on Nusa Penida's southwest coast, is renowned for its resident Manta ray colony, making it a must-visit dive site. Divers of all levels are drawn to its diverse range of underwater experiences, including reef exploration, photography, training, and fish identification. Notable species found here include the day octopus and the tawny nurse shark, both captivating creatures. Manta rays, particularly the Manta alfredi species, gracefully glide through the water with their distinctive pectoral fins and are often seen at cleaning stations, where cleaner fish help them rid parasites. However, these majestic creatures face threats from overfishing and human impacts. Manta Point offers an extraordinary underwater adventure, showcasing the beauty and diversity of marine life in this region.

programme.title: The Komodo dragons of south Rinca, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Horseshoe Bay is located in the south of Rinca island, it is formed by Rinca island in the north and Nusa Kode in the south. The area is well known to be one of the best place to see wild Komodo dragons. The Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis), also known as the Komodo monitor, is a member of the monitor lizard family Varanidae that is endemic to the Indonesian islands of Komodo, Rinca, Flores, and Gili Motang. It is the largest extant species of lizard, growing to a maximum length of 3 metres, and weighing up to approximately 70 kilograms. As a result of their size, Komodo dragons are apex predators, and dominate the ecosystems in which they live. Komodo dragons hunt and ambush prey including invertebrates, birds, and mammals. It has been claimed that they have a venomous bite; there are two glands in the lower jaw that secrete several toxic proteins. The biological significance of these proteins is disputed, but the glands have been shown to secrete an anticoagulant. Komodo dragons' group behavior in hunting is exceptional in the reptile world. The diet of Komodo dragons mainly consists of Javan rusa (Rusa timorensis), though they also eat considerable amounts of carrion. Komodo dragons also occasionally attack humans.

programme.title: Lawa Darat island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Lawa Darat island is located in the northern part of the Komodo National Park. Also known as the “island close to the land” has a barren, desert savannah that changes color from green to yellow depending on the season. The island features easy hiking trails and two viewpoints to suit both spectacular sunrise and sunsets. Lawa Darat island is well protected from strong winds and waves, making the island the perfect spot for various activities to be carried out in safety. Some even refer to the island as the Komodo’s fjord, as attributed to its geological position. Besides, Lawa Darat island’s proximity to the ocean crossroads enables visitors to experience unexpected marine surprises such as encountering the humpback or the blue whale emerging majestically from the sea. The main attraction of Lawa Darat island is the scenic view that awaits visitors as they trek and reach the peak. This sole reason is what drives most Komodo National Park visitors to land on this island. Although beautiful all day long, the best recommended time to trek to the peak is sunset, when the breathtaking panoramic view calls for an Instagram selfie. The vantage point makes it perfect for capturing the beautiful beaches or the rolling hills catching rays of light. Trekking to the peak of the island might be considered as quite challenging for some, in particular, the beginners, but it is incredibly doable and worthwhile. The view is better and more beautiful as you trek higher where the reef becomes clearer while the mountainside begins to glow. Be ready for the remarkable panorama that awaits you at the top where the Komodo National Park lies in the opposite.

programme.title: Dive Site Manta Alley, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Manta Alley dive site is located at the far southern end of Komodo Island in the Indian Ocean. Manta Alley consists of a series of small rocky islands a few hundred meters away from the main island. There are several spots around these rocks where mantas can be found almost all year round. The site starts in a shallow reef close to the shore, where you can expect a strong to mild drift dive. You should keep your eyes wide open just as you enter the water, as mantas can be often found right in the shallows. Manta Rays are coming to this area for mating and cleaning purposes, where small wrasse and butterfly fish clean the mantas of parasites. The cleaning station is around 20 meters, where the rocks meet a white sandy bottom, perfect spot to watch mantas gliding into the rocks. Though mantas are the main attraction of this site, Manta Alley it is also full of marine life including reef sharks, schools of trevallies and large wrasses. The corals are very beautiful and diverse as well, making this spot a spectacular background for marine life photography.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Maravilla, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Maravilla is located 10 kilometers west of Puerto Morelos. The cenote is a sinkhole in the shape of a bell, where the entrance is a hole in the middle of the top. The thick sulfur cloud offers views that look from another planet. Getting close to this cloud is necessary to observe the gorgeous living stalactites, the biothems often called “Hell’s bells.” Those mysterious rock formations are alive and grow underwater thanks to extraordinary endemic bacteria. This type of speleothems, called “elephant feet,” has been found in only 4 cenotes, all in the Puerto Morelos area and are subject to ongoing scientific research.

programme.title: Dive Site Siaba Kecil, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Siaba Kecil dive site is located in the Central part of the Komodo National Park. The best time to dive this site is when the current is running! This is a real rollercoaster of a ride and will often be referred to as the 'Superman drift'. This gorgeous coral reef with a stunning overhang has a fast moving current - nothing scary just a great drift along. No need to kick! Towards the end of the dive site you drift towards and more sheltered area and the current eases off. Here you can relax (catch your breath!), and admire the stunning hard corals and thousands on anthias. This is also a great spot for seeing hawksbill turtles. The strong currents of this dive site attract large fish including giant trevally, barracuda, tuna, sharks and the odd ray too! The overhangs provide a fascinating topography and if the current allows they are great to explore and hunt for nurse sharks, bamboo sharks and other bizarre creatures.

programme.title: Batu Bolong north, Komodo, Indonesia
programme.desc: You are about to go on a fascinating journey through the amazing underwater world of Batu Bolong. As you watch this remarkable documentary, you will discover the wonderful beauty and diversity of life below the waves. Located within Indonesia's Komodo National Park, Batu Bolong's exposed rock pinnacle reveals a hidden paradise full of marine wonders. Despite challenges like changing currents and depths, you will learn how expert divers navigate the currents and explore different depths, from shallow coral gardens to tall walls. You will see the vibrant underwater dance of reef fish, including colorful groupers, moray eels, and majestic emperor fish. You will encounter the mysterious white tip reef shark, marvel at its unique anatomy, and understand its interesting behaviors. As the documentary reveals the top predator, the giant trevally, you will be captivated by its striking features and hunting skills. You will delve into the complex relationships within the ecosystem, from cleaner fish caring for their companions to the vital role of table corals in sheltering marine life. Immerse yourself in this kaleidoscope of colors, shapes, and behaviors, and let the enchanting beauty of Batu Bolong's underwater world leave you longing for more, ready to return to this aquatic oasis time and again.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Angelita, Tulum, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Angelita is located 10 kilometers west of Tulum. Angelita is a magical cenote that is often described as mysterious and a bit spooky. At first, the cenote appears to be unassuming, just a small pond in the middle of a very thick jungle. However, the deepest parts of the cenote go down to 204 ft (66 m). Its most amazing feature is a 4.5 ft (1.5 m) thick hydrogen sulfide cloud that starts at 83 ft (27 m). This cloud is made up of gases that have leaked out of decomposing trees and leaves that fall from the jungle into the cenote. This gas accumulates where the fresh and the salt water meet (the halocline). This creates a false floor at the bottom, which can be traversed to reach a dark, otherworldly chamber that is full of jungle detritus. The base of this mountain of detritus starts below but reaches above the cloud. Rising again from below the cloud, the peak of the mountain of detritus takes on a new face, as if one is ascending a cloud-topped mountain. On the way out of the cenote, there is a small cave loop, and at the surface, one can get an appreciation for all of the trees that provide this cenote with its hydrogen sulfide cloud.

programme.title: Dive Site Paradise Reef, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Paradise Reef dive site is located in the west of Cozumel. Paradise Reef is the first reef when entering the Marine Park. The current runs from south to north normally. You will start across from the entrance to the Caleta and drift north. There are 2-3 coral ridges that parallel the shoreline. You can see schools of Grunts, Snappers, and Sergeant Majors, many Queen Angelfish. There are nice coral heads ranging from 3-6m tall that jut out from a sandy bottom. You can find anemones, and an assortment of nice sponges clinging to the coral heads. Just about every kind of fish from the area can be found here. Some of the bigger animals include barracuda and grouper. Keep a close eye for the small denizens such as Spotted Drum, Smooth Trunkfish, Spotted Moray Eels, and Spiny Lobster.

programme.title: Lawalaut Island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Lawalaut Island is located northeast of Gili Lawa Darat Island. Gili Lawa Laut is understandably a magnet for visitors on land and sea. The island is in the Lesser Sunda Islands and sits to the north of Komodo Island and the other small islet of Gili Lawa Daret and as such is protected as part of the Komodo National Park. Geologically the islets are volcanic like much of the region and they have beautiful hills popular with hikers who come for the stunning views and secluded beaches. The island is uninhabited but has numerous trails for walking up the hills to see the surrounding area. The wildlife above water is slightly less of a draw than the sea life on this island as there is less vegetation than in other areas. The hills are grassy though, and the landscape is very beautiful and a popular photography spot for visitors to the national park.

programme.title: Arborek Island, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: Arborek is a tiny island in Raja Ampat archipelago, on west Papua. It is easily walkable on foot, taking roughly thirty minutes to walk the entire coastline. The island is known for its very hospitable tourism village and exceptional handicrafts with a thriving souvenir community. Be ready to be greeted with open arms by everyone, with many children who are eager to be photographed. This authentic island welcomes guests with pride, the islanders are happy to introduce all to the Papuan culture and unique traditional foods. It is a perfect paradise to learn a bit of the Asai culture, which is still kept alive in this isolated place. Arborek island, traditionally a mooring spot for boatmen, is surrounded by splendid sago palms, nourished by fish and it is sparsely populated by a tiny population of around 200 residents, spread in around 40 families. The water is crystal clear, with white fine sand and many coconut trees and bushes, providing a quite comforting and refreshing atmosphere. At the wooden pier you will find some gazebos, ideal for relaxing.

programme.title: Dive Site Yucab, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Yucab dive site is located in front of Mia beach in the west of Cozumel. There is a huge concentration of marine life which covers this reef. There are sponges everywhere and of every color. The sand scoured overhangs offer refuge for lobsters, banded coral shrimps and the arrow crab. There are also large numbers of squirrelfish, angel and butterflyfish always swimming in pairs. This is a great site for photographers.

programme.title: Dive Site Paso Del Cedral, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Paso Del Cedral dive site is located in front of El Cedral in the south west of Cozumel. Also called Cedral Wall it is one of the most beautiful dive sites in Cozumel. It can be done as a wall dive or closer to shore over the reef. The part of the reef that is not a wall, consists of a mile of sloping hills covered in sponges and coral. The reef bottoms out at about 18 meters (60 feet). As for the current, it's generally moderate to strong. As you drift you'll get to see eagle rays, lobsters, hawksbill turtles, green morays, big pufferfish, toadfish, and even sharks.

programme.title: Reynolds City
programme.desc: Tracer, a hit man with emotional issues, is on a job to collect from a client when it goes sour. programme.title: Dive Site San Clemente, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: San Clemente dive site is located in the south west of Cozumel. San Clemente Reef is a beginner diver's dream, with shallow depth between 10 meters and 15 meters and little current. As it is located between the Yucab Reef and the Tormentos Reef, San Clemente shares plenty of similarities with these two dive sites. Divers can encounter here spotted moray eels, butterflyfish swimming in pairs, groupers, snappers, grunts, scorpionfish, angelfish, seahorses hidden in the grass, damselfish, cowfish, eagle rays, filefish, barracudas. This dive spot has a mostly sandy bottom with coral outcrops and patches.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Zapote, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Zapote is located 20 kilometers west of Puerto Morelos. Cenote Zapote is named after the Sapote trees growing nearby. It is located on the “Ruta de los Cenotes” the old road from Puerto Morelos to Valladolid. Zapote has quite a deep drop from the land surface to the water surface of 6m/20ft but its access is easy via stairs. The walls will rise above you like a fortress and once you start your descent they become narrower until a depth of 20m/66ft before starting to open back up again. Once you reach a depth of 30m/100ft you will be above the talus cone in a bell shaped chamber with a narrow skylight in the top through which you just descended. Halocline and a thin misty layer of Hydrogen Sulfide floating on top of it, as well as some of the most amazing and incredible formations commonly described as bells, elephant feet, shower heads or trumpets will truly take your breath away with their strange beauty and impressive size.

programme.title: Dive Site Saporkren at Night, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: The village of Saporken is located on the island of Waigeo, close to the capital town of Waisai. This site is typically dived at night, however day diving is good too. Saporkren is your typical sandy bottom muck dive site, which is a little grubby since its just off of the village jetty. Making your way down a gentle slope (with little or no current) past a few coral bommies, the best bit of Saporkren is generally around 12-20 metres. We found full-size seahorses, cute bobtail squid, flying flatworms, clownfish anemones, colemani shrimp plus many unusual crabs species such as the boxer, xeno and porcelain.

programme.title: Padar island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Padar island is located in the middle of the straight between Rinca and Komodo Island. Padar is the third largest island in the Komodo National Park. It is located in the south central of the park, between Komodo and Rinca Island. In the past, Padar was one of the island in Komodo where there were dragons live. Along with the illegal hunting activities by human being, they are slowly disappeared and almost unable to see them anymore. The cause is simply because of the lack of foods, like deer and wild boar. Their extinction can be because they just died alone without any food to eat or prolonged hunger or they can be migrated to nearest island, Rinca. The island now remains empty with no dragons. However, other wild animals such as wild boars are still around daily. Today, Padar has become one of the most popular place to visit in Indonesia. It offers super magnificent view from the top of the island with pink sandy beach on the west side and white sandy beach on the east side. Formation of towering hill, just like Jurassic park. Although the island has no dragons existed, the island is one of the best charming spot of trekking. Those who love photographic, this is perhaps the best place for spectacular photos.

programme.title: Dive Site C56 Shipwreck, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: C-56 Shipwreck dive site is located in Puerto Morelos. The C-56 shipwreck served in World War II and it was sold to the Mexican Marine in 1966. The time pass by and later on 28th Oct 2000 was purposefully sunk, as a new attraction for divers coming to the Riviera Maya. Laying perfectly upright, with the keel on the sand at 90ft, the 184ft long Mexican Gun Boat was quickly inhabited by various marine life. The deck, at 64ft, is teeming with life and it's common to see a large shoal of Big Eye Travellies hunting there. As we travel around the wreck we commonly see large Wrasse, Groupers, Morays and, looking up, flights of Eagle Rays. Soft corals have colonized the wreck and now offer a home to many Arrow crabs and Fire worms amongst other small crustaceans and invertebrates.

programme.title: Sumidero Canyon, Tuxtla Gutiérrez , Mexico
programme.desc: Sumidero Canyon is located just north of the city of Tuxtla Gutiérrez. Sumidero Canyon (Spanish: Cañón del Sumidero) is a deep natural canyon which creation began around the same time as the Grand Canyon in the U.S. by a crack in the area's crust and subsequent erosion by the Grijalva River, which still runs through it. Sumidero Canyon has vertical walls which reach as high as 1,000 metres, with the river turning up to 90 degrees during the 13 kilometre length of the narrow passage.

programme.title: Dive Site Batu Bolong South, Komodo National Park, Indonesia Trailer
programme.desc: Embark on an amazing journey to explore the wonders of Batu Bolong south, a remote and enchanting diving location in Komodo National Park. Dive into crystal-clear waters with excellent visibility to encounter a vibrant array of marine life and stunning underwater landscapes. However, navigating the challenges of strong currents and varying depths requires careful preparation and diving experience. From the captivating giant trevally to the intricate social structures of anthias, you'll observe fascinating behaviors and adaptations of the underwater world's inhabitants. The documentary also sheds light on the unique coral reefs, their crucial symbiotic relationships, and the serious threats they face. This highlights the urgent need for conservation efforts to protect these vital underwater ecosystems often referred to as the "rainforests of the sea." Ultimately, this episode provides a captivating and educational glimpse into the incredible marine life and underscores the importance of preserving these precious underwater environments.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Dos Ojos, Tulum, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Dos Ojos is located 15 kilometers north of Tulum. Dos Ojos (Two Eyes) refers to two neighboring cenotes that are connected by a large cavern that also connects to a subterranean river. The original explorations of this water system, one of the largest in the world, started in the Dos Ojos cenotes. The total length of the combined system was measured at 310.95 kilometers (193.22 mi). This cenote dive site consists of two independent circuits: The first dive starts at the Barbie Line, a 415 meters line with wide spaces and large light galleries. The second dive circuit is called the Bat Cave, a very different experience. The Bat Cave is an adjacent cenote, next to Dos Ojos, and represents a much more preserved environment, mainly due the fact that the roof of the cenote hasn’t collapsed yet and all of the formations around it are in very good shape.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Creekside Cigar Co.
programme.desc: In this episode, Dave and BG chat with Darren Joffrey of Principal Cigars, discussing the unique concept behind his "Boy Band Volume One" cigar project, where five master blenders created cigars inspired by Nina Simone's album "I Put a Spell on You". programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Des Racines et des ailes - Passion Patrimoine
programme.sub-title: Sur les rives de la Garonne
programme.desc: Des Pyrenees espagnoles ou elle prend sa source, au vaste estuaire de la Gironde ou elle se jette, la Garonne parcourt plus de 600 kilometres a travers le Comminges, l'Agenais ou l'Entre-deux-Mers. Le fleuve evolue au cours de ce long voyage. L'apport de ses affluents, comme la Neste, l'Ariege, le Tarn et le Lot, modifie son visage. A bord d'un helicoptere, Didier Taillefer part en Espagne pour faire des photos aeriennes de l'une des principales sources du fleuve : le Trou du Toro. Ce site exceptionnel est situe au pied du massif de la Maladeta, ou la Garonne disparaît sous terre avant de reapparaître au Val d'Artan. Au coeur des Pyrenees, le fleuve donne naissance a un jardin de Cocagne : le Comminges. Dans le village de Huos, Remy Martin a amenage un verger-potager bio sur un ancien meandre.

programme.title: Amor Musical
programme.desc: Todo inicia cuando son transferidos a la escuela Jung San que recibe auspicio por parte de una fundación millonaria y poderosa. Como es de esperarse, los días escolares en esta escuela se convierte en una lucha sin fin. Cada día enfrentan el gran abismo entre el rico y el pobre. Ante la cruda realidad, en lo único que pueden confiar es en su música. Tocar con sus amigos es la única cosa que los mantiene vivos, al mismo tiempo, Su música los hace brillar por encima de los demás. “Amor Musical” es un drama musical como nunca antes visto; al mejor estilo y creado para el sentimiento punk.

programme.title: Le Grand Inventaire de la Planète: Arctique Canadien

Les membres de l'expédition The Explorers partent à la découverte de l'Arctique canadien, une région emblématique du bouleversement climatique qui touche notre planète. Pour être au plus près d'une civilisation et d'une nature en pleine mutation, pour témoigner de l'évolution de la vie sur ces terres glaciales, l'expédition a parcouru le Grand Nord Canadien, du printemps au début de l'hiver.

programme.title: Forhold på 4 hjul - Små raske biler
programme.desc: Her møter vi mennesker og deres kjærlighet for ikke typiske motorsporter. I hver episode vil vi treffe to personer som driver med samme motorsport. Vi følger dem hjemme før vi blir med dem på et arrangement der de konkurrerer mot hverandre.

programme.title: Garasjen - Kim Jannike sin BMW, Grensetreffet i Halden og nytt eksosanlegg!
programme.desc: Kim Jannike har bygget seg en BMW, og denne skal brukes i drifting, men når hun skal prøvekjøre bilen med Asgeir går ikke alt som planlagt. Det er også tid for Grensetreffet i Halden, hvor det er mange flotte biler å se på.

programme.title: Garasjen - Spesiell drømmebil, Finnskogfestivalen og en låve full av amcar
programme.desc: I denne episoden av Garasjen er det klart for Finnskogfestivalen. Der møter vi Line Myrvold og Leif André Ødegaard som skal konkurrere i bilcross og rallycross. Torbjørn viser oss også hans noe spesielle drømmebil.

programme.title: Garasjen - Nyinnkjøpt Ferrari, Volvo 142 og finale på Finnskogfestivalen
programme.desc: Vi møter vi Ivar og Asgeir. De har kjøpt en Volvo 142, som de skal bygge om til en rask rallybil for å delta i Rallye Monte-Carlo Historique. I Drammen treffer vi Arild Olsen som har kjøpt en Ferrari han ikke har sett på nett.

programme.title: Garasjen - Mekking av både Ferrari og Volvo 142, og et lite lakk kurs
programme.desc: Halvor Sunde fra Risør åpner dørene til sin egen garasje, som blant annet huser en strøken Hotrod. Asgeir besøker Arild og hans Ferrari, og gir ham en hjelpende hånd når motoren skal settes inn. Videre går turen til Gatebil on ice i Sigdal.

programme.title: Milestones - Milestones 1980-1990
programme.desc: 80-tallet er preget av racinglegender. En ny verdensmester kommer på banen, og viser frem motorer med 1.200 hester. Porche 959 er den raskeste landeveisbilen i verden. Motorsport har mer å si enn noen gang, og tiårene er fyllt med store motorer.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Porsche Taycan im E-Auto-Supertest
programme.desc: Porsche hat den Taycan umfangreich überarbeitet und in vielen Disziplinen verbessert. Die Batterie wird größer und kann schneller Laden. Alex Bloch fährt den Basis Taycan mit großer Batterie im E-Auto-Supertest und kommt aus dem Grinsen nicht mehr raus. Wie die Chancen stehen, dass der Taycan auf die Pole Position der Elektroautos fährt, seht ihr im Video.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der MG4 Electric im E-Auto Supertest
programme.desc: Der MG4 schwimmt auf der Erfolgswelle! Der Überflieger befindet sich unter den Top 5 der meistverkauften Elektroautos in Deutschland. Was der chinesischen Kompaktstromer im Vergleich zum Opel Astra Electric und dem VW ID.3 drauf hat, klärt Alexander Bloch.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Opel Astra Electric im EAS
programme.desc: Kein anderes Auto hat Alexander Bloch bisher in ein solches Wechselbad der Gefühle geschmissen. Von „sensationell!“ bis „macht ihr Witze?“ ist alles dabei. Was die Stärken und Schwächen des Opel Astra Electric sind und ob er sich gegen den VW ID.3 behaupten kann, erfahrt ihr hier!

Alexander Bloch testet den neuen Taycan 4 auf Eis und Schnee. Wie macht sich der Allrad und vor allem: Wie lädt der Elektro-Sportwagen bei -20 Grad?

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - 8 Fakten zu Lackschutzfolien
programme.desc: Steinschläge, Lackkratzer und die Launen der Natur können das Aussehen und den Wert eines Autos erheblich beeinträchtigen. Doch es gibt eine Lösung, die nicht nur schützt, sondern auch stylisch ist: die Autofolierung. Alex erklärt welche Unterschiede es gibt und was es bei einer Folierung zu beachten gibt. Mit Drahtbürste, Steinschleuder und Gabelstapler macht Alex außerdem den Extrem-Haltbarkeitstest einer Lackschutzfolie.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Citroën ë-C3: Nur günstig? Oder auch gut?
programme.desc: Alexander Bloch checkt den neuen Citroën ë-C3. Mit einem Basispreis von 23.300 Euro zählt er zu den günstigsten E-Autos am Markt. Aber ist er nur billig oder auch wirklich sein Geld wert? Alexander Bloch macht den Test und zeigt auch die Unterschiede zum C3-Verbrenner und zum Konkurrenten Dacia Spring.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Cupra Tavascan VZ: Wieder der gleiche MEB-Brei?
programme.desc: Alexander Bloch testet den neuen Cupra Tavascan VZ - erneut ein E-Auto auf dem MEB. Auf diesem Baukasten stehen bereits VW ID.4, Skoda Enyaq & Co. - Was ist gleich, was ist anders und was überrascht?

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Renault Scenic E-Tech
programme.desc: Im Jahr 1996 betrat der erste Renault Mégane Scénic den Markt und gliederte sich im Segment der kompakten Vans ein. Aus Megane und Scenic entwickelten sich zwei eigenständige Baureihen. Welche Qualitäten der neue Scenic E-Tech im Vergleich zu seinem kleinen Bruder hat, findet Alex Bloch heraus.

programme.title: Brace For Impact - Indagine Ad Alta Quota
programme.desc: Tensione alle stelle in questo thriller che vede l'esperta di disastri aerei Sofia coinvolta in un'indagine per far chiarezza sulle reali cause di un tragico incidente in cui ha perso la vita il fratello. Il suo desiderio di giustizia la porterà a infrangere le regole del servizio di intelligence e a scoprire un complotto terroristico.

programme.title: Break - Trappola Di Ghiaccio
programme.desc: Un gruppo di amici è pronto a celebrare la notte di Capodanno dentro una funivia, ma quella che doveva essere un'indimenticabile avventura si tramuta presto in un incubo senza fine. Quando la funivia si rompe inaspettatamente, i ragazzi rimangono sospesi nel vuoto a tremila metri di altezza. La paura della morte li porterà a fare di tutto per sopravvivere, tra cui mostrare la loro vera natura.

programme.title: Empire Of The Sharks
programme.desc: Adrenalinico sci-fi scritto e diretto da Mark Atkins (Jurassic School) e sequel di Planet of the Sharks. In un futuro dove il 98% della superficie terrestre è sott’acqua, uno spietato signore della guerra governa grazie al suo esercito di super squali. Solo una ragazza con il potere psichico di comunicare con gli squali tenterà di opporsi, per sconfiggere il tiranno e liberare la sua gente.

programme.title: Sky Sharks
programme.desc: Cyber squali volanti cavalcati da supersoldati mutanti nazisti, attaccano un aereo di linea con l'intento di uccidere i passeggeri. Che la guerra abbia inizio!

programme.title: 40 Days And Nights - Apocalisse Finale
programme.desc: Se un imponente spostamento tettonico causasse uno tsunami di proporzioni enormi, quale sarebbe l'unica soluzione? Recuperare l'insegnamento di Noè e della sua arca e costruire un'enorme nave capace di contenere solo cinquantamila persone, più il DNA di tutte le specie esistenti al mondo, cercando così di salvarle da una tempesta apocalittica.

programme.title: Bestie Dall'abisso - Il Giorno Del Giudizio
programme.desc: 15 anni prima le creature demoniache provenienti dal sottosuolo invasero la Terra con l'obiettivo di eliminare completamente il genere umano. Ricordato come il Giorno del Giudizio dai sopravvissuti di quell'infernale olocausto, l'umanità riuscì a prevalere. Le creature ora son tornate. Una famiglia cerca di difendersi e di richiudere l'ingresso che permette ai mostri di raggiungere il pianeta.

programme.title: Android Cop
programme.desc: Il futuro delle forze dell'ordine. Nel 2045, un poliziotto e il suo partner androide entrano nella Zona, una sezione proibita della città abitata dalla popolazione colpita da una malattia sconosciuta. Insieme scopriranno perché la malattia si è diffusa e, con tutta la tecnologia a loro disposizione, cercheranno di bloccarne il contagio.

programme.title: Martian Land - Tempesta Su Marte
programme.desc: Nel futuro, la razza umana si è trasferita su Marte e vive in città simili a quelle terrestri, ma protette da enormi campi di forza. Quando una gigantesca tempesta di sabbia sfonda la cupola e distrugge completamente Mars New York, gli abitanti di Mars Los Angeles dovranno cercare di fermare la tempesta, prima di essere i prossimi ad essere spazzati via.

programme.title: Age Of Tomorrow
programme.desc: La Terra è invasa da Ufo che distruggono tutto quello che si muove. Mentre la battaglia infuria, un gruppo di astronauti riesce a entrare nella nave principale dove uno di loro scopre un portale che conduce al mondo degli alieni. Riesce appena ad avvertire qualcuno dei suoi superiori sulla Terra, prima che tutto il gruppo venga ucciso. Parte l'ultimo disperato tentativo per fermare l'invasione.

programme.title: Attacco Alieno Su Los Angeles
programme.desc: Nel Febbraio del 1942 un oggetto non identificato cade su Los Angeles. Settant'anni dopo gli alieni tornano per completare l'attacco attraverso una grande navicella spaziale atterrata sulla città. Le forze armate di Los Angeles rimangono sconvolte in quanto i loro missili non rispondono più ai comandi. Chi la spunterà?

programme.title: Apocalypse Earth - Apocalisse Sulla Terra
programme.desc: In seguito a un'invasione aliena, un gruppo di umani disperati fuggono dalla Terra e arrivano in un pianeta lontano. I rifugiati si ritroveranno ben presto a dover combattere per la propria sopravvivenza contro feroci e ostili creature.

programme.title: Nature Next Door
programme.sub-title: Nature Next Door - Antarctique, à la Voile entre les Icebergs
programme.desc: Nous suivons des voiliers et un photographe qui naviguent vers l'Antarctique, dans une région où le seul prédateur terrestre est le skua antarctique. Parmi les phoques et les otaries, les manchots empereurs et les baleines à bosse, nous pouvons constater que la relation entre notre espèce et celles qui vivent dans cet univers polaire n'est plus aussi sombre qu'elle l'était autrefois.

programme.title: Nature Next Door
programme.sub-title: Nature Next Door - Islande, sur la Piste du Renard Polaire
programme.desc: C'est une île posée sur un océan glacial, créée par les volcans, sculptée par les glaciers et les cascades. Au cœur de l'été, cette île accueille des millions d'oiseaux, qui malgré leur apparence légère sont incroyablement résistants. Au nord de cette île, on se lance dans une quête : rencontrer et filmer le seul mammifère originaire d'Islande.

programme.title: Nature Next Door
programme.sub-title: Nature Next Door - Costa Rica, le Royaume des Colibris

Des oiseaux multicolores, des reptiles un peu moins discret, mammifères plutôt curieux, partout se livre un fabuleux spectacle de la nature.

programme.title: Auto China: Driving future of mobility
programme.desc: Auto China 2026 opens on April 24, showcasing nearly 1,500 vehicles over 10 days – at a pivotal turning point for China's automotive industry. Amid commodity volatility and fractured supply chains, electrification is no longer a question of “if” but “how fast.” As the world’s largest electric vehicle (EV) market and a major force of global EV sales, how is China shaping the pace and direction of this charge towards greener, smarter vehicles? Join us on BizTalk this week as we explore how China and Germany are moving in step toward the next phase of the future of mobility.

programme.title: Global Business-American Edition
programme.desc: Global Business is the flagship business show of CGTN English Channel, bringing you the latest economic data, business trends and policies.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha — the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Our lens turns to the "Xiangjiang Ladies" who work in Changsha’s high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city’s innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha’s distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: The Art of Harmony: Human Becoming
programme.desc: “The Art of Harmony” is a documentary about Confucianism, produced by CGTN and Discovery Channel. It highlights the timeless nature of the sage’s philosophy and its global relevance today. Join us in exploring how the world might benefit from the pursuit of “The Art of Harmony”.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programme.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programme.title: Young star on green field
programme.desc: Meet Sun Chenxi, a 12-year-old soccer "star" from Ningbo who first picked up the game at the age of four and is already playing with the confidence of a veteran. Sun says he dreams of turning pro one day and leading China's men's team to the World Cup. Dribbling and passing with skills far more advanced than his age, he has won over audiences far and wide after his father posted clips of Sun flashing his fancy footwork on social media. The soon-to-be-teenager now has millions of followers online. Already recognized as a rising young talent, high hopes are pinned on Sun as he is cheered on by his parents, friends, and throngs of fans online.

programme.title: Celadon Ou Music
programme.desc: Celadon ou music is also called "bowl music.” The reason is that the ancient Chinese word for bowl sounds like ou. The music originated simply as improvised rhythms tapped out on bowls. It was this spontaneity that made celadon ou so popular. Celadon ou music was at the height of its popularity over 1,100 years ago. But with time, it faded from history. At one point, it was even on the verge of being lost forever. After hundreds of years of obscurity, it re-emerged at the end of last century.

programme.title: Kesi
programme.desc: Silk is a classic symbol of Chinese culture. It helped opened up economic and cultural exchanges between East and West and witnessed the spread of Eastern civilization to the world. As a representative of traditional Chinese silk art, kesi is renowned for its highly ornamental weaving techniques of highlighting warps and breaking wefts, and has been deeply loved by people for thousands of years. In folk culture, it enjoys the reputation of “an inch of kesi is worth an inch of gold.”

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: CULTURAL INHERITORS Inheritance matters more than fame
programme.desc: The Vibe production team's meticulously crafted documentary series "Cultural Inheritors". The eight episodes span across various regions of China, focusing on the inheritors and artists of intangible cultural heritage. They explore and innovate with artisanal dedication, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship of fields such as the Ru Kiln porcelain, colored stone inlay, Pu'er tea, and Lingnan woodwork. Let’s embark on a cultural journey together, savoring the beauty of tradition and embracing the spirit of intangible cultural heritage!

programme.title: Miao Silverware: A Shining Epic
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the fascinating world of the silver-working art of the Miao ethnic group. Join us, and hear the stories and see the works of four remarkable individuals. From a national-level inheritor who is preserving the traditional craft, to an artist infusing personal flair into his designs; from a female silversmith imbuing her work with feminine warmth, to a young artisan inspiring a new generation, we investigate the rich heritage, cultural significance, and evolving potential of Miao silverware.

programme.title: Xinjiang On the Road
programme.desc: Join an international group on an ice-snow adventure across northern Xinjiang, exploring stunning winter scenery, rich ethnic culture and warm hospitality from Urumqi to Altay.
